sources.publisher: Embassy of Grenada in the United States

sources.title: Immigration and Visas
sources.publisher: Embassy of Panama in the United States
sources.officialityEvidence: Panama's live Embassy page publishes the ordinary nationality no-visa list, expressly includes Bosnia and Herzegovina, and states a three-month visitor maximum for that cohort.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No Visa RequireD: IF you are from ... Bosnia and Herzegovina

policies.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina biometric civil passports: Grenada visa at entry
policies.summary: Grenada's currently linked country schedule directly assigns Bosnia and Herzegovina to Port of Entry, defined as a visa granted on arrival.
conditions: Applies to the ordinary biometric civil passport identified by Bosnia and Herzegovina's passport authority and to short visitor travel.
Grenada defines Port of Entry as a visa granted on arrival; its separate prior-to-arrival, diplomatic, official, work, residence, cruise and other-document routes are outside this classification.
The active Embassy schedule is updated April 2024 and should be rechecked if Grenada publishes a later country schedule. Final admission remains a border decision.

policies.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina biometric civil passports: Dominican Republic advance visa
policies.summary: The Dominican Republic's current official Tourist Card list expressly requires tourists from Bosnia and Herzegovina to obtain a visa at a Dominican diplomatic mission instead of entering with a Tourist Card.
conditions: Applies to short tourism using an ordinary biometric civil Bosnia and Herzegovina passport.
Obtain the visa through a Dominican diplomatic mission before travel; the Tourist Card route does not apply to the expressly listed nationality.
Work, study, residence, diplomatic, official, special-document and final-admission treatment are outside this classification.

policies.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina biometric civil passports: Panama visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Panama's live Embassy nationality list expressly includes Bosnia and Herzegovina in its no-visa ordinary visitor cohort.
conditions: Applies to short visitor travel using an ordinary biometric civil Bosnia and Herzegovina passport, for up to three months as stated by the official list.
The separate waiver based on a qualifying third-country visa or residence permit is conditional and is not needed for this named no-visa rule.
Work, residence, diplomatic, official, other-document and final-admission conditions remain outside this classification.

conflicts.explanation: Grenada's active Embassy schedule directly assigns Bosnia and Herzegovina to Port of Entry and defines that category as a visa granted on arrival.
The Dominican Republic's current official list names Bosnia and Herzegovina among tourists who cannot use the Tourist Card and must obtain a consular visa.
